fields.title: 2 Papers Accepted at the 46th IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP) 2021
fields.excerpt: Two papers from our research team have been accepted at ICASSP 2021! The accepted works focus on sensor calibration and scalable matrix factorization, highlighting our contributions to signal processing for modern sensing and data environments.
fields.content:
We are proud to announce that two of our papers have been accepted for presentation at the 46th IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP) 2021, one of the leading international conferences in signal processing.

1. In situ calibration of cross-sensitive sensors in mobile sensor arrays using fast informed non-negative matrix factorization

Authors: O. Vu Thanh, M. Puigt, F. Yahaya, G. Delmaire, and G. Roussel

This paper addresses the challenge of calibrating mobile sensor arrays composed of heterogeneous and cross-sensitive sensorswhere each sensor's reading is influenced by others in the same array. The work introduces a novel in situ calibration approach based on the informed factorization of a partially observed non-negative matrix. The proposed method leverages a fast informed (semi-)NMF algorithm, offering an efficient and scalable solution for real-time sensor calibration in the field.

2. Random Projection Streams for (Weighted) Nonnegative Matrix Factorization

Authors: F. Yahaya, M. Puigt, G. Delmaire, and G. Roussel

This paper proposes a new framework for applying random projections to Weighted Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (WNMF), especially when dealing with missing data entriesa common scenario in large-scale datasets. The method introduces a principled way to incorporate data confidence (via weights) and demonstrates substantial computational gains in speeding up NMF algorithms, particularly when used with Nesterov's method or alternating least squares. The approach makes NMF more scalable and practical for modern big data environments.

fields.title: 1 paper presented at the international Traveling Workshop on Interactions between low-complexity data models and Sensing Techniques (iTWIST) 2020
fields.excerpt: Were excited to share a third accepted ICASSP 2021 paper, where we propose a scalable randomized EM algorithm for Weighted NMF using bilateral structured projectionsideal for large-scale and incomplete data analysis.
fields.content:
Authors: F. Yahaya, M. Puigt, G. Delmaire, and G. Roussel

This paper presents a randomized version of the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm tailored for Weighted Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (WNMF), particularly in contexts with missing or uncertain data. The proposed approach introduces bilateral structured random projections into the EM framework, significantly reducing computational complexity while preserving performance.

By compressing both dimensions of the data matrix before factorization, this method offers a scalable solution to large-scale WNMF problems, especially in applications such as recommender systems and sensor networks. The authors demonstrate that the randomized EM algorithm achieves competitive accuracy compared to full-resolution methods but with substantially lower computational cost.

fields.title: 1 Paper Accepted at the 27th European Signal Processing Conference (EUSIPCO) 2019
fields.excerpt: Our work on matrix factorization with missing data has been accepted at EUSIPCO 2019! This paper proposes an efficient method that blends weighted NMF with advanced optimization techniques to handle incomplete and large-scale datasets.
fields.content:
Weighted NeNMF for Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with Missing Data

Authors: F. Yahaya, M. Puigt, G. Delmaire, and G. Roussel

This paper addresses the challenge of performing Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) when some entries in the data matrix are missing or uncertaina common situation in real-world applications like sensor networks, medical imaging, and recommender systems.

The proposed method extends NeNMF (Nesterov-accelerated NMF) to a weighted setting, allowing it to naturally handle missing data via a confidence weight matrix. The approach combines the speed of Nesterovs gradient-based updates with the flexibility of weighted factorization, resulting in a robust, scalable, and fast algorithm. Experimental results show improved performance compared to conventional NMF approaches on both synthetic and real datasets.

fields.biography_content: Dr. Farouk Yahaya is a researcher and engineer with interests in matrix factorization, glottal inverse filtering, source separation, low-rank models, and sensor calibration. He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Universit du Littoral Cte dOpale (2021), and was previously a postdoctoral researcher at INRIA Bordeaux University of Bordeaux working on pathological speech analysis. He is currently a Senior ML/AI Engineer at Expleo Group France.
